a: Idea 33's sample engine on two stages (assumed masses)
Aster tools/slice12-research/data/dla-oracle-m1-vectors.json (62ddb17): 99942 Apophis, departure 2026-07-02, TOF 677.177 d, M=1 left branch, poliastro-matched to 5.7e-13 deg
S-type: Itokawa's bulk silicate water, 160–510 ppm (all of it, an upper bound)

refusals: No engine dry mass is computed or given here: the fetched sources (SP-8107, SP-8110, SP-8120, TM-107318) give turbopump weights, not engine weights.
A sourced engine dry mass for module 34 (Stack), from the engine's data sheet or the vehicle's mass breakdown.
Gravity, drag and steering losses, and so the orbit this stack reaches, are not computed here: that needs an ascent trajectory.
Module 35 (Max Q) flies this vehicle through the 1976 atmosphere.
This vehicle's drag coefficient is the Saturn V's (the only wind-tunnel curve here), scaled by its diameter.
A wind-tunnel or CFD axial-force curve for this vehicle's shape.
Open-loop steering: the orbit reached is what this pitch plan gives, not a target orbit.
Module 36 (Closed Loop) flies the same vehicle to a chosen orbit with guidance.
Guidance cut Stage 2 off with 4929.9 kg unburned, but idea 34's vehicle gives that stage no second burn: whether it can restart for a departure is not stated.
A second burn for this stage in idea 34 (a restartable engine, with its coast losses), or a separate departure stage.
Navigation is perfect here: guidance knows the true state. The flight's own cutoff was 30.8 m and 0.20 m/s from its prediction (section 9.3).
An inertial-platform error model (ST-124M drift and accelerometer errors) to fly guidance on a navigated state.
The dispersion sizes are one flight's deviations from its prediction (AS-512), used as one sigma: a population of flights is not in the report.
MSFC's three-sigma dispersion tables for Saturn V (the operational trajectory documents), or the deviations of several flights.

The 1143.3 kg left in the Stage 2 buy at most 189 m/s (ideal rocket equation, J-2 vacuum exhaust velocity 4146 m/s, no gravity loss) against the 3247 m/s an impulsive burn needs for this C3: this vehicle cannot make this departure from this launch (short by 3060 m/s before any finite-burn loss).
More upper-stage propellant or a lighter payload (module 34), a lower C3 (module 39), or a launch azimuth nearer due east.
Nutation and UT1 - UTC are not modelled: the pole and sidereal time are IAU 2006 mean values (measured against the full IAU 2006/2000A model: README), and UT1 is taken as UTC.
IERS Earth orientation parameters (UT1 - UTC, polar motion) for the date, and a nutation series.
No dogleg: the parking orbit's plane passes through the pad at liftoff. Outside the corridor a dogleg or a plane change at departure would cost performance this page does not compute.
A yaw-steering ascent model (idea 36 can fly one if its target plane is moved off the pad).

The finite burn needs 13935 kg of propellant and the Stage 2 has 1143.3 kg (short by 12792 kg): burned to empty it reaches C3 -57.62 km^2/s^2, an orbit with apogee 880.7 km, not the 0.5114 the transfer needs.
More propellant in the stage (module 34) or a lower C3 (module 39): no payload, however light, gets there on this propellant.
Even with no payload the stage cannot reach C3 0.5114 km^2/s^2: its 1143.3 kg of propellant on its own 14517 kg give at most 314.3 m/s against the 3247 m/s an impulsive burn needs.
More propellant in the stage (module 34), or a lower C3 (module 39).

No start or cutoff transient and no venting: the engine runs at its deck's vacuum thrust from ignition to cutoff, and nothing boils off in the coast. On Apollo 17 the start and cutoff transients gave 811.8 and 205.8 kN s, and the S-IVB vented 1041 kg of hydrogen in its 3 h coast (MPR-SAT-FE-73-1 sections 7.6, 7.8, Table 16-9).
Transient and venting models for this engine and stage.
The asymptote handed on has J2 followed out to 20 Earth radii but not the Moon or the Sun: their pull on the way out of the Earth's sphere of influence is not in it.
A propagation with the Moon and the Sun out of the Earth's sphere of influence (module 40).
Idea 38 hands on no hyperbolic departure state (its refusals say why), so there is no flown departure to carry along this transfer: the transfer shown is the one the chain set out to fly.
A departure that closes in idea 38 (more propellant, a lighter payload, or a lower C3).

Patched conics: the transfer starts at Earth's centre at the departure epoch and ends at the asteroid's, about the Sun alone. Earth's and the Moon's pull on the way out, the planets on the way, and solar radiation pressure are not in it.
An n-body propagation of the transfer (module 40).

Sunlight is not modelled: no spacecraft area per mass is given (the chain has no spacecraft yet). It is not small: JPL's OSIRIS-APEX predict, flown here without it, drifts 9,400 km from JPL's in 200 days of 2026 (it fits 0.013 m^2/kg, oracle), and a TCM can absorb it only if it is modelled.
The spacecraft's sunlit area, mass and reflectivity (set the area per mass here).

The asteroid's own orbit uncertainty is not mapped to the arrival: the spacecraft is delivered relative to where Aster's elements put it, and the approach (optical navigation) that cuts the target's uncertainty is module 42's.
The orbit's covariance from JPL's Small-Body Database, and approach optical navigation (module 42).
27 Delta-DOR baseline sessions found no hour with both stations above 10 deg: the spacecraft's declination puts it out of their common sky.
Another agency's antennas for a north-south baseline (ESA, as Lucy's paper notes), or fewer sessions.
The chain has no spacecraft yet: this radio is Dawn (asteroids Vesta and Ceres)'s (DESCANSO article 13), not this mission's.
The mission's own transponder, amplifier, antenna and coding (a telecom design control table).
The command uplink is not computed: the sources give no HGA receive gain and receiver noise for these presets, so command rates and uplink margins are not stated.
The spacecraft receiver's noise temperature and the HGA receive gain (an uplink DCT).
61 day(s) (2026-07-03 to 2029-04-21) put more than -85 dBm into the 34-m receiver, the recommended maximum (810-005 104 Table 7): the high-gain antenna is too loud so close to the Earth.
A low-gain antenna or the station's low-gain mode (-65 dBm) for those days.
99942 Apophis (2004 MN4)'s mass has not been measured: GM 2.68 m^3/s^2 is the OSIRIS-APEX team's estimate (1.36 to 4.37). Orbits and hover costs near it move with it.
A radio-science mass from a spacecraft at the body (as OSIRIS-REx measured Bennu's; OSIRIS-APEX will measure Apophis's).

NEAR Shoemaker as built carried 318 kg of propellant (1450 m/s); this approach needs 4273 m/s, so the tanks are sized to 1654 kg with the dry mass held at 487 kg, which understates a real redesign (bigger tanks weigh more).
A spacecraft designed for this arrival, or a transfer with a smaller arrival v-infinity (idea 39).
Gravity is a point mass: 99942 Apophis (2004 MN4)'s shape and spin are not in it, so orbits within a few radii are not right here.
A shape model and density (module 43, Lumpy).

The chain has no spacecraft yet: the engine is NEAR Shoemaker's (NSSDCA: 450 N, 1450 m/s from 318 kg on 487 kg dry, so 294.2 s effective), the sunlit area per mass OSIRIS-APEX's (AAS 24-063: 81.119 kg/m^2).
The mission's own spacecraft: dry mass, tanks, engines and their specific impulse, sunlit area.

Uniform density: the field is the shape filled evenly. At Bennu the measured field (Scheeres et al. 2020, Table 1) has J2 2.7% and J3 15.8% larger than its constant-density shape gives, surface gravity differs by up to ±3% and slopes by ±1°, and the constant-density stable equilibrium is unstable in the measured field.
A measured gravity field: radio tracking from orbit (OSIRIS-REx at Bennu; OSIRIS-APEX at Apophis from 2029).

Apophis's tumbling needs inertia ratios 0.61 and 0.965 (Pravec et al. 2014); the radar shape filled evenly gives 0.730 and 0.947. Uniform density cannot be the whole truth (or the shape is off), so the field beyond GM carries that doubt.
A shape from OSIRIS-APEX imaging and a measured field.
99942 Apophis (2004 MN4) tumbles (Pravec et al. 2014): no frame turns with it at a constant rate, so its field never stands still in one and it has no equilibrium points or rotational Roche lobe.
Nothing: they do not exist for a tumbler. Hovering costs Delta-v everywhere (idea 42's station-keeping).
The shape's plates are 25 m across: slopes and gravity under a lander's footprint (metres) are not resolved, and slopes here are smoother than at that scale (Bennu's 3 m model averages 17°).
The descent and back-away need 0.946 m/s, 0.160 kg of propellant at Isp 294.2 s; the chain's spacecraft reaches the stand-off with 0.103 kg (idea 42's mass block).
More propellant at launch (idea 42's tankage), a lighter spacecraft, or a slower departure leg.

The site is a 105 m^2 plate of idea 43's 25 m shape: boulders, craters and slopes at the scale of the 8 m safe radius and the 0.32 m sampler head are not in it, so the chance of an unsafe contact is not computed (only the chance of landing inside the safe radius).
A local terrain model from OSIRIS-APEX imaging, then a hazard map.
The regolith's resistance is Bennu's at Nightingale (inferred from NASA's 48.8 cm in ~6 s at 10 cm/s), carried to 99942 Apophis (2004 MN4) as an analog: nothing has touched its surface.
The spacecraft's accelerometer record of the contact (Walsh et al. 2022, Sci. Adv.) or, for another body, a touch.

No particle-size map of 99942 Apophis (2004 MN4) exists, and TAGSAM-class collection depends on the smallest and largest particles and their size distribution (Walsh et al. 2022); the sample mass is not computed. The Nightingale analog below is labelled as such.
Imaging at better than 1 cm/pixel of the site (OSIRIS-APEX), then the sampleability algorithm.

Anchors that rely on the ground's strength (harpoons, screws) are not modelled: Bennu's near surface is "loosely packed and lightly bound" (NASA, 2022), and no strength is known for 99942 Apophis (2004 MN4). Holding down is by weight and thrust only.
A measured cohesion or an anchor pull test in situ.

For an S-type the water is the 160–510 ppm Itokawa's returned grains carry in their pyroxene and olivine (Jin and Bose 2019), all of it counted: how much an oven at 750 °C releases from nominally anhydrous minerals is not measured in these sources, so every water number here is an upper bound.
A heating experiment on an ordinary chondrite (LL) or on Itokawa grains, with the water measured against temperature and time.

Digging resistance is idea 44's fit to OSIRIS-REx's 10 cm/s contact at Bennu (69–165 Pa), used as the pressure on a drum's cut face; nothing has been excavated in milligravity, and the drums' own forces were measured only in lunar simulant at 1 g (IPEx), where the vertical force was the weight of the regolith caught: whether a cut lifts a lander that weighs millinewtons is not measured, and not modelled here.
An excavation test in the target's regolith, or in a simulant on a reduced-gravity flight, with the vertical force measured.
The horizon is the site plate's own plane: shadows from boulders and the rest of the body are not cast (idea 43's shapes have 25 m plates). Set a horizon mask to be conservative.
A terrain model at metre scale and a ray-traced horizon.

Digging 10.0 mm deep pushes the spacecraft 33.6 mN sideways (the drums' cutting imbalance and the dug regolith brought to its speed); with the slope's own 5.7 mN along the ground the feet need a friction coefficient of 0.86 against 45.8 mN of weight on the ground (0.13 for the slope alone). No friction is measured for this regolith, so whether the feet slip is not judged.
A friction coefficient for the feet on this regolith (set one here as a what-if), or propellant to cancel the sideways push with thrust.
Idea 45's water is an upper bound (all of Itokawa's 510 ppm counted as released), so every propellant figure here is an upper bound too.
A measured water release for this asteroid's rock (idea 45's "release" refusal).
The electrolyser's mass, and its pumps, dryers and power conditioning, are not on file (DOE gives $/kW and kWh/kg, not kg/kW); it is assumed to stay on the asteroid and is not in the return dry mass.
A flight electrolyser's mass per kW (the ISS OGA's, for instance).

Array power is scaled as 1/r² from its 1 au value, ignoring cell temperature: checked only beyond 1 au, where it reads 7.0 % low for NEAR at 2.2 au and 3.5 to 17 % low for Psyche; this stay is inside 1 au, where hotter cells make it likely optimistic.
The array's measured power against Sun distance and temperature.

Delivered Isp is the shifting ideal times 0.9791, the RL10A-3-3's published/ideal at O/F 5 (SP-8120 Table I). At O/F 7.94 that factor is carried, not measured; no flown hydrogen-oxygen engine on file runs there.
Hot-fire data for a hydrogen-oxygen engine at this mixture ratio.
Cryogenic tank walls, insulation blankets and supports are not given a mass (they are set by minimum gauge and structure, not by pressure, and none are on file); their volumes and areas are computed.
A small flight cryogenic tank's mass per litre.
The heat leak is MHTB's 45-layer insulation on an 18 m³ tank, 0.22 W/m² at 305 K; tanks this small (11.3 L of hydrogen) leak more per m² through supports and pipes, so boil-off here is a lower bound.
Heat-leak data for a tank of this size.
No 90 K cryocooler's measured efficiency or mass is on file: the 90 K stage is costed at 13.95 % of Carnot (the 20 K unit's at full lift, NASA/Creare 2026), 16.73 W per W, and given no mass.
A flight 90 K cryocooler's measured input power and mass (NASA's 150 W class).
There are no batteries: coolers and electrolyser run only while the Sun is up at the site, and the tanks boil in the dark.

The asteroid's orbit is Aster's elements (epoch 2026-05-01 TDB) integrated through idea 40's forces, without Yarkovsky or asteroid perturbers and without its orbit uncertainty. JPL's NHATS return legs, computed with JPL's own ephemerides, are the check (this page's reality table): the gap grows after an Earth encounter.
JPL's SPK for the body and its covariance (Horizons, or the Small-Body Database).
The asteroid's own gravity is left out of the departure burn and the craft leaves from its centre of mass.
The escape speed from the stand-off (idea 43's field) added to the burn.

The return's navigation is not analysed: the departure burn carries Aster's 10 % margin and one correction the size of its own 3-sigma execution error (Lucy's 30 mm/s + 4 %, idea 40); orbit-determination errors and the TCMs that cut them are not budgeted. The correction's propellant is counted as burned with the departure burn; kept for a correction made later, its hydrogen (0.0286 kg) would boil away in 2.8 days at the passive rate, so a later correction needs the coolers held or a separate storable thruster.
A covariance analysis of the return like idea 40's for the outbound (its 116.6 m/s was mostly the launcher's injection error, which does not apply here).
No structure, container or heat shield is counted for the material: the craft's dry mass is idea 46's, and whatever holds the material home (and protects it at entry, module 49) is not on file.
A container and capsule mass (OSIRIS-REx's and Hayabusa2's capsules are the flown references).
Arriving at 12.53 km/s at 125 km, above NHATS's 12 km/s entry limit: as handed on, it needs braking, aerocapture or a catch.
Module 48 (Catch) compares the options; or brake here to the limit (NHATS's rule).

Idea 47 aims at a 123.7 km perigee, above the air (it ends at 86 km here): a flyby. Entering at -6.502° needs a perigee at 56.44 km (B 87.71 km nearer). A correction 14 days out costs about 79.8 mm/s, 184 g of propellant; 0 kg arrives.
Set module 47's aim perigee to 56.44 km, so the departure burn aims at the entry (no correction at the Earth).
No heat shield, structure or container mass is counted: the entry mass is the arrival mass (9565.4 kg) inside the chosen shape.
Module 49 (Hot Return) sizes the heat shield from this heating; a container mass for the material.

Heating is Sutton & Graves's convective stagnation-point rate only ("Radiative heating was neglected", NASA TR R-376). At lunar-return speeds radiation is not small: "radiative heating is approximately one-third of the total heating rate" for Apollo (NASA TN D-6843).
A radiative correlation or a shock-layer solution (module 49).

The atmosphere is the 1976 standard to 86 km and none above; no winds, no day-of density. OSIRIS-REx's team saw "atmospheric density being much lower than was Earth-GRAM was predicting" (OSIRIS-REx EDL performance, 2025).
A day-of atmosphere (GEOS forecast, GRAM dispersions) for the entry date.

The vehicle's numbers are partly assumed: stagnation-point radius = half the diameter, the convention of the Apollo heating analysis (NASA TN D-6843: "radius, 6.417 feet (one-half the maximum diameter)"), before its spherical-segment adjustment, which is not on file.
The vehicle's own aerodynamic database and heat-shield geometry.

Constant bank, no guidance: the corridors are the lift-up and lift-down bounds a guided vehicle flies between, wider than what a guidance law and its dispersions leave (the TransHab study flew bank reversals to hold its target).
An entry guidance law with dispersions (Monte Carlo over density, aerodynamics and the entry state).

No winds and no day-of atmosphere: the descent under the parachutes drifts with the wind (Stardust's 50 m/s northward wind moved its landing), and OSIRIS-REx's whole descent ran faster than every model (its own reconstruction included).
A forecast atmosphere and winds for the landing day (GEOS, as OSIRIS-REx's team recommends).
No landing site is chosen: the touchdown point is wherever this entry state leads (-29.35°, 94.621°), and the ground is taken at 0 m (sea level). A recovery needs a range under the footprint.
Re-target idea 47's arrival (its time and aim) so the footprint falls on a recovery range such as UTTR, and set the ground altitude here.

The parachutes are sized here, not designed: the drag areas scale the SRC's canopies (same ballistic coefficient under the drogue as Stardust's, the main for 4.5 m/s at the ground) at the SRC canopies' drag coefficients; 171 OSIRIS-REx mains' worth of drag area. Canopy loads, cluster interference, mass and packing are not modelled.
A parachute design for this mass (a cluster like Apollo's), with its own drag and opening-load data.
Opening loads assume the canopy's drag area grows linearly over OSIRIS-REx's measured filling times (0.38 s drogue, 1.14 s main); no canopy opening-load data are on file.

Thickness: this entry is outside Stardust's heat-shield design (heat load 77 kJ/cm² over its 36.5; stagnation pressure 0.764 atm over its 0.5), so its 5.82 cm does not carry over, and sizing a new thickness needs PICA's in-depth thermal model: "Material properties of high-performance ablators are subject to export-control restrictions" (Milos & Chen). Only the recession (10.3 mm at the stagnation point) is a lower bound.
PICA's property model (PICAv3.3, available to qualified U.S. persons) and a material-response code (FIAT), or an entry inside Stardust's design.
Pyrolysis gas and the char layer are not modelled: the mass lost is the surface recession only (the phenolic's gases leave too), and the bondline temperature is not computed.
An in-depth material-response model (see the thickness refusal).
notes: Idea 31 at O/F 2.6 (the chain's O/F 2.6 (idea 31's committed sample)), 10 MPa.

blockers.what: The departure stage runs dry 12,792 kg of propellant short of the burn (13,935 kg needed, 1,143.3 kg left in orbit). Everything from idea 39 on flies a departure that did not happen.
Idea 42 sizes the tanks for the approach and station-keeping only; the touch-and-go needs 0.16 kg and 0.103 kg is left.

value.summary: Lands on paper, but does not close: departure, tag propellant.

verdict.source: mission.js mission(): halts, seams of severity "breaks", and whether idea 49 landed

value.event: Cruise begins (idea 40's patched conic; nothing departed)
Stay ends: 7.11 kg of propellant made
The asteroid's own Earth pass (38,010 km)

mass_ledger.source: each module's masses at its events

value.note: idea 36's guided ascent to Aster's parking orbit, less its losses
needed, not flown: the stage runs dry 12,790 kg short

durations.source: differences of the timeline's TDB epochs

value.what: The rocket departs with 10,000 kg of payload; the spacecraft idea 42 sizes for this arrival weighs 2,141.3 kg at launch.
value.what_would_help: Pick a rocket that carries the spacecraft (the closed loop: chain-sc or as512-sc).

value.what: The departure stage runs dry 12,792 kg of propellant short of the burn (13,935 kg needed, 1,143.3 kg left in orbit). Everything from idea 39 on flies a departure that did not happen.
value.what_would_help: A bigger upper stage, a lighter payload, or a rocket with the capability (the launcher chart).

value.what: Idea 36 flies to a 28.5° parking orbit; idea 37 re-flies the ascent on the window's 35° azimuth (59.7°) and reaches orbit with a different mass.
value.what_would_help: Nothing: idea 37 is the one that lines the orbit up with the asymptote; the mass it reaches is the one carried.

value.what: The cruise starts 9.9 h after the departure point the window put the burn at (idea 40 departs on idea 39's patched conic at Aster's cell time).
value.what_would_help: A departure that idea 38 flies, so idea 40 starts from its state.

value.what: The arrival speed flown through the planets differs from the conic's.
value.what_would_help: Nothing: idea 40's flown arrival is the one idea 42 brakes from.

value.what: Idea 42 sizes the tanks for the approach and station-keeping only; the touch-and-go needs 0.16 kg and 0.103 kg is left.
value.what_would_help: Size the tanks for the touch-and-go too (the what-if's toggle).

value.what: Idea 46 adds 105.6 kg of coolers to the dry mass at the asteroid that the spacecraft idea 42 launched did not carry (and the electrolyser and tanks are refused, not weighed).
value.what_would_help: Launch the plant: the what-if adds its mass to the outbound dry mass.

value.what: The 8,972.7 kg of material rides home with no container, structure or heat-shield mass booked: idea 48 calls the whole 9,565.4 kg an Apollo-derived capsule and refuses the heat-shield mass.
value.what_would_help: A return vehicle design (capsule structure, heat shield, parachutes) in the dry mass; idea 49 gives the parachute area it would need.

value.what: Idea 41 plans the link for 677 days of cruise and a 364-day stay; the stay flown is 110 days and the 167-day way home has no link budget at all.
value.what_would_help: Idea 41 run on the return leg (it reads a cruise from idea 40; idea 47's return is not in that form).

value.what: No flown heat shield covers this entry (heat load 2.11 times Stardust's design); the thickness, and so the shield's mass, is refused.
value.what_would_help: PICA's thermal properties (export-controlled) or arc-jet tests at this heat load.

seams.units: kg, s, m/s, days, refusals (per seam)
seams.source: mission.js seams(): where a link starts from something other than what the previous one ended with

refusals.reason: The touch-and-go needs 0.16 kg of propellant and 0.103 kg is left after the approach (idea 42 sizes the tanks without it).
refusals.what_would_help: Size the tanks for the touch-and-go too.

refusals.reason: This rocket cannot reach the C3 even with no payload: its departure stage runs dry 12,792 kg short with the payload it carried, and idea 38 finds no payload that works.
refusals.what_would_help: A bigger rocket: pick one of Aster's launch-vehicle curves.

assumptions: The water made (idea 45) and so the propellant (idea 46) are held: the dig was limited by its oven, not by the spacecraft's weight, on the chain; a different mass could change that.
Idea 49's ablation (27.45 kg) is held: a heavier capsule flies a different entry.

refusals.reason: The asteroid's own orbit uncertainty is not mapped to the arrival: the spacecraft is delivered relative to where Aster's elements put it, and the approach (optical navigation) that cuts the target's uncertainty is module 42's.
refusals.what_would_help: The orbit's covariance from JPL's Small-Body Database, and approach optical navigation (module 42).

refusals.reason: 27 Delta-DOR baseline sessions found no hour with both stations above 10 deg: the spacecraft's declination puts it out of their common sky.
refusals.what_would_help: Another agency's antennas for a north-south baseline (ESA, as Lucy's paper notes), or fewer sessions.

refusals.reason: The chain has no spacecraft yet: this radio is Dawn (asteroids Vesta and Ceres)'s (DESCANSO article 13), not this mission's.
refusals.what_would_help: The mission's own transponder, amplifier, antenna and coding (a telecom design control table).

refusals.reason: The command uplink is not computed: the sources give no HGA receive gain and receiver noise for these presets, so command rates and uplink margins are not stated.
refusals.what_would_help: The spacecraft receiver's noise temperature and the HGA receive gain (an uplink DCT).

refusals.reason: 61 day(s) (2026-07-03 to 2029-04-21) put more than -85 dBm into the 34-m receiver, the recommended maximum (810-005 104 Table 7): the high-gain antenna is too loud so close to the Earth.
refusals.what_would_help: A low-gain antenna or the station's low-gain mode (-65 dBm) for those days.

refusals.reason: 99942 Apophis (2004 MN4)'s mass has not been measured: GM 2.68 m^3/s^2 is the OSIRIS-APEX team's estimate (1.36 to 4.37). Orbits and hover costs near it move with it.
refusals.what_would_help: A radio-science mass from a spacecraft at the body (as OSIRIS-REx measured Bennu's; OSIRIS-APEX will measure Apophis's).

refusals.reason: NEAR Shoemaker as built carried 318 kg of propellant (1450 m/s); this approach needs 4273 m/s, so the tanks are sized to 1654 kg with the dry mass held at 487 kg, which understates a real redesign (bigger tanks weigh more).
refusals.what_would_help: A spacecraft designed for this arrival, or a transfer with a smaller arrival v-infinity (idea 39).

refusals.reason: Gravity is a point mass: 99942 Apophis (2004 MN4)'s shape and spin are not in it, so orbits within a few radii are not right here.
refusals.what_would_help: A shape model and density (module 43, Lumpy).

refusals.reason: The chain has no spacecraft yet: the engine is NEAR Shoemaker's (NSSDCA: 450 N, 1450 m/s from 318 kg on 487 kg dry, so 294.2 s effective), the sunlit area per mass OSIRIS-APEX's (AAS 24-063: 81.119 kg/m^2).
refusals.what_would_help: The mission's own spacecraft: dry mass, tanks, engines and their specific impulse, sunlit area.

refusals.reason: Uniform density: the field is the shape filled evenly. At Bennu the measured field (Scheeres et al. 2020, Table 1) has J2 2.7% and J3 15.8% larger than its constant-density shape gives, surface gravity differs by up to ±3% and slopes by ±1°, and the constant-density stable equilibrium is unstable in the measured field.
refusals.what_would_help: A measured gravity field: radio tracking from orbit (OSIRIS-REx at Bennu; OSIRIS-APEX at Apophis from 2029).

refusals.reason: Apophis's tumbling needs inertia ratios 0.61 and 0.965 (Pravec et al. 2014); the radar shape filled evenly gives 0.730 and 0.947. Uniform density cannot be the whole truth (or the shape is off), so the field beyond GM carries that doubt.
refusals.what_would_help: A shape from OSIRIS-APEX imaging and a measured field.

refusals.reason: 99942 Apophis (2004 MN4) tumbles (Pravec et al. 2014): no frame turns with it at a constant rate, so its field never stands still in one and it has no equilibrium points or rotational Roche lobe.
refusals.what_would_help: Nothing: they do not exist for a tumbler. Hovering costs Delta-v everywhere (idea 42's station-keeping).

refusals.reason: The shape's plates are 25 m across: slopes and gravity under a lander's footprint (metres) are not resolved, and slopes here are smoother than at that scale (Bennu's 3 m model averages 17°).
refusals.what_would_help: OSIRIS-APEX's imaging shape model (2029).

refusals.reason: The descent and back-away need 0.946 m/s, 0.160 kg of propellant at Isp 294.2 s; the chain's spacecraft reaches the stand-off with 0.103 kg (idea 42's mass block).
refusals.what_would_help: More propellant at launch (idea 42's tankage), a lighter spacecraft, or a slower departure leg.

refusals.reason: The site is a 105 m^2 plate of idea 43's 25 m shape: boulders, craters and slopes at the scale of the 8 m safe radius and the 0.32 m sampler head are not in it, so the chance of an unsafe contact is not computed (only the chance of landing inside the safe radius).
refusals.what_would_help: A local terrain model from OSIRIS-APEX imaging, then a hazard map.

refusals.reason: The regolith's resistance is Bennu's at Nightingale (inferred from NASA's 48.8 cm in ~6 s at 10 cm/s), carried to 99942 Apophis (2004 MN4) as an analog: nothing has touched its surface.
refusals.what_would_help: The spacecraft's accelerometer record of the contact (Walsh et al. 2022, Sci. Adv.) or, for another body, a touch.

refusals.reason: No particle-size map of 99942 Apophis (2004 MN4) exists, and TAGSAM-class collection depends on the smallest and largest particles and their size distribution (Walsh et al. 2022); the sample mass is not computed. The Nightingale analog below is labelled as such.
refusals.what_would_help: Imaging at better than 1 cm/pixel of the site (OSIRIS-APEX), then the sampleability algorithm.

refusals.reason: Anchors that rely on the ground's strength (harpoons, screws) are not modelled: Bennu's near surface is "loosely packed and lightly bound" (NASA, 2022), and no strength is known for 99942 Apophis (2004 MN4). Holding down is by weight and thrust only.
refusals.what_would_help: A measured cohesion or an anchor pull test in situ.

refusals.reason: For an S-type the water is the 160–510 ppm Itokawa's returned grains carry in their pyroxene and olivine (Jin and Bose 2019), all of it counted: how much an oven at 750 °C releases from nominally anhydrous minerals is not measured in these sources, so every water number here is an upper bound.
refusals.what_would_help: A heating experiment on an ordinary chondrite (LL) or on Itokawa grains, with the water measured against temperature and time.

refusals.reason: Digging resistance is idea 44's fit to OSIRIS-REx's 10 cm/s contact at Bennu (69–165 Pa), used as the pressure on a drum's cut face; nothing has been excavated in milligravity, and the drums' own forces were measured only in lunar simulant at 1 g (IPEx), where the vertical force was the weight of the regolith caught: whether a cut lifts a lander that weighs millinewtons is not measured, and not modelled here.
refusals.what_would_help: An excavation test in the target's regolith, or in a simulant on a reduced-gravity flight, with the vertical force measured.

refusals.reason: The horizon is the site plate's own plane: shadows from boulders and the rest of the body are not cast (idea 43's shapes have 25 m plates). Set a horizon mask to be conservative.
refusals.what_would_help: A terrain model at metre scale and a ray-traced horizon.

refusals.reason: Digging 10.0 mm deep pushes the spacecraft 33.6 mN sideways (the drums' cutting imbalance and the dug regolith brought to its speed); with the slope's own 5.7 mN along the ground the feet need a friction coefficient of 0.86 against 45.8 mN of weight on the ground (0.13 for the slope alone). No friction is measured for this regolith, so whether the feet slip is not judged.
refusals.what_would_help: A friction coefficient for the feet on this regolith (set one here as a what-if), or propellant to cancel the sideways push with thrust.

refusals.reason: Idea 45's water is an upper bound (all of Itokawa's 510 ppm counted as released), so every propellant figure here is an upper bound too.
refusals.what_would_help: A measured water release for this asteroid's rock (idea 45's "release" refusal).

refusals.reason: The electrolyser's mass, and its pumps, dryers and power conditioning, are not on file (DOE gives $/kW and kWh/kg, not kg/kW); it is assumed to stay on the asteroid and is not in the return dry mass.
refusals.what_would_help: A flight electrolyser's mass per kW (the ISS OGA's, for instance).

refusals.reason: Array power is scaled as 1/r² from its 1 au value, ignoring cell temperature: checked only beyond 1 au, where it reads 7.0 % low for NEAR at 2.2 au and 3.5 to 17 % low for Psyche; this stay is inside 1 au, where hotter cells make it likely optimistic.
refusals.what_would_help: The array's measured power against Sun distance and temperature.

refusals.reason: Delivered Isp is the shifting ideal times 0.9791, the RL10A-3-3's published/ideal at O/F 5 (SP-8120 Table I). At O/F 7.94 that factor is carried, not measured; no flown hydrogen-oxygen engine on file runs there.
refusals.what_would_help: Hot-fire data for a hydrogen-oxygen engine at this mixture ratio.

refusals.reason: Cryogenic tank walls, insulation blankets and supports are not given a mass (they are set by minimum gauge and structure, not by pressure, and none are on file); their volumes and areas are computed.
refusals.what_would_help: A small flight cryogenic tank's mass per litre.

refusals.reason: The heat leak is MHTB's 45-layer insulation on an 18 m³ tank, 0.22 W/m² at 305 K; tanks this small (11.3 L of hydrogen) leak more per m² through supports and pipes, so boil-off here is a lower bound.
refusals.what_would_help: Heat-leak data for a tank of this size.

refusals.reason: No 90 K cryocooler's measured efficiency or mass is on file: the 90 K stage is costed at 13.95 % of Carnot (the 20 K unit's at full lift, NASA/Creare 2026), 16.73 W per W, and given no mass.
refusals.what_would_help: A flight 90 K cryocooler's measured input power and mass (NASA's 150 W class).

refusals.reason: There are no batteries: coolers and electrolyser run only while the Sun is up at the site, and the tanks boil in the dark.
refusals.what_would_help: A battery and its mass.

refusals.reason: The asteroid's orbit is Aster's elements (epoch 2026-05-01 TDB) integrated through idea 40's forces, without Yarkovsky or asteroid perturbers and without its orbit uncertainty. JPL's NHATS return legs, computed with JPL's own ephemerides, are the check (this page's reality table): the gap grows after an Earth encounter.
refusals.what_would_help: JPL's SPK for the body and its covariance (Horizons, or the Small-Body Database).

refusals.reason: The asteroid's own gravity is left out of the departure burn and the craft leaves from its centre of mass.
refusals.what_would_help: The escape speed from the stand-off (idea 43's field) added to the burn.

refusals.reason: The return's navigation is not analysed: the departure burn carries Aster's 10 % margin and one correction the size of its own 3-sigma execution error (Lucy's 30 mm/s + 4 %, idea 40); orbit-determination errors and the TCMs that cut them are not budgeted. The correction's propellant is counted as burned with the departure burn; kept for a correction made later, its hydrogen (0.0286 kg) would boil away in 2.8 days at the passive rate, so a later correction needs the coolers held or a separate storable thruster.
refusals.what_would_help: A covariance analysis of the return like idea 40's for the outbound (its 116.6 m/s was mostly the launcher's injection error, which does not apply here).

refusals.reason: No structure, container or heat shield is counted for the material: the craft's dry mass is idea 46's, and whatever holds the material home (and protects it at entry, module 49) is not on file.
refusals.what_would_help: A container and capsule mass (OSIRIS-REx's and Hayabusa2's capsules are the flown references).

refusals.reason: Arriving at 12.53 km/s at 125 km, above NHATS's 12 km/s entry limit: as handed on, it needs braking, aerocapture or a catch.
refusals.what_would_help: Module 48 (Catch) compares the options; or brake here to the limit (NHATS's rule).

refusals.reason: Idea 47 aims at a 123.7 km perigee, above the air (it ends at 86 km here): a flyby. Entering at -6.502° needs a perigee at 56.44 km (B 87.71 km nearer). A correction 14 days out costs about 79.8 mm/s, 184 g of propellant; 0 kg arrives.
refusals.what_would_help: Set module 47's aim perigee to 56.44 km, so the departure burn aims at the entry (no correction at the Earth).

refusals.reason: No heat shield, structure or container mass is counted: the entry mass is the arrival mass (9565.4 kg) inside the chosen shape.
refusals.what_would_help: Module 49 (Hot Return) sizes the heat shield from this heating; a container mass for the material.

refusals.reason: Heating is Sutton & Graves's convective stagnation-point rate only ("Radiative heating was neglected", NASA TR R-376). At lunar-return speeds radiation is not small: "radiative heating is approximately one-third of the total heating rate" for Apollo (NASA TN D-6843).
refusals.what_would_help: A radiative correlation or a shock-layer solution (module 49).

refusals.reason: The atmosphere is the 1976 standard to 86 km and none above; no winds, no day-of density. OSIRIS-REx's team saw "atmospheric density being much lower than was Earth-GRAM was predicting" (OSIRIS-REx EDL performance, 2025).
refusals.what_would_help: A day-of atmosphere (GEOS forecast, GRAM dispersions) for the entry date.

refusals.reason: The vehicle's numbers are partly assumed: stagnation-point radius = half the diameter, the convention of the Apollo heating analysis (NASA TN D-6843: "radius, 6.417 feet (one-half the maximum diameter)"), before its spherical-segment adjustment, which is not on file.
refusals.what_would_help: The vehicle's own aerodynamic database and heat-shield geometry.

refusals.reason: Constant bank, no guidance: the corridors are the lift-up and lift-down bounds a guided vehicle flies between, wider than what a guidance law and its dispersions leave (the TransHab study flew bank reversals to hold its target).
refusals.what_would_help: An entry guidance law with dispersions (Monte Carlo over density, aerodynamics and the entry state).

refusals.reason: No winds and no day-of atmosphere: the descent under the parachutes drifts with the wind (Stardust's 50 m/s northward wind moved its landing), and OSIRIS-REx's whole descent ran faster than every model (its own reconstruction included).
refusals.what_would_help: A forecast atmosphere and winds for the landing day (GEOS, as OSIRIS-REx's team recommends).

refusals.reason: No landing site is chosen: the touchdown point is wherever this entry state leads (-29.35°, 94.621°), and the ground is taken at 0 m (sea level). A recovery needs a range under the footprint.
refusals.what_would_help: Re-target idea 47's arrival (its time and aim) so the footprint falls on a recovery range such as UTTR, and set the ground altitude here.

refusals.reason: The parachutes are sized here, not designed: the drag areas scale the SRC's canopies (same ballistic coefficient under the drogue as Stardust's, the main for 4.5 m/s at the ground) at the SRC canopies' drag coefficients; 171 OSIRIS-REx mains' worth of drag area. Canopy loads, cluster interference, mass and packing are not modelled.
refusals.what_would_help: A parachute design for this mass (a cluster like Apollo's), with its own drag and opening-load data.

refusals.reason: Opening loads assume the canopy's drag area grows linearly over OSIRIS-REx's measured filling times (0.38 s drogue, 1.14 s main); no canopy opening-load data are on file.
refusals.what_would_help: The canopy's drop-test opening-load factor.

refusals.reason: Thickness: this entry is outside Stardust's heat-shield design (heat load 77 kJ/cm² over its 36.5; stagnation pressure 0.764 atm over its 0.5), so its 5.82 cm does not carry over, and sizing a new thickness needs PICA's in-depth thermal model: "Material properties of high-performance ablators are subject to export-control restrictions" (Milos & Chen). Only the recession (10.3 mm at the stagnation point) is a lower bound.
refusals.what_would_help: PICA's property model (PICAv3.3, available to qualified U.S. persons) and a material-response code (FIAT), or an entry inside Stardust's design.

refusals.reason: Pyrolysis gas and the char layer are not modelled: the mass lost is the surface recession only (the phenolic's gases leave too), and the bondline temperature is not computed.
refusals.what_would_help: An in-depth material-response model (see the thickness refusal).

refusals.reason: The mission does not close: The departure stage runs dry 12,792 kg of propellant short of the burn (13,935 kg needed, 1,143.3 kg left in orbit). Everything from idea 39 on flies a departure that did not happen. Idea 42 sizes the tanks for the approach and station-keeping only; the touch-and-go needs 0.16 kg and 0.103 kg is left.
refusals.what_would_help: The what-if on this page, or the modules the blockers name.

assumptions: Every number is the module's that owns it, read from its handoff (the source of each is given); this module adds the order, the sums, the seams and the what-if.
Times are TDB seconds past J2000 with TDB - UTC = 69.184 s (Aster's offset for this span), as every module uses.
The what-if holds every link except the spacecraft mass it changes: windows, delta-v, water, propellant made and the entry are the chain's.
